checks: The mean value theorem supplies an interior α with φ′(α) nonzero. Every cap fraction of the constructed body lies in (0,1), because a ball about the origin contributes positive volume on either side of every cut.
The witness uses k=d−1≥1 and A=−sign(φ′(α))I. The realization is analytic at its actual centered, stationary orientation and supplies arbitrarily large positive multiplier while p_K(u)=α stays fixed.

For a unit tangent w the support function extended to R^d is convex. On u+τw its expression is sqrt(1+τ²) times g on the great circle at angle arctan τ. At zero these factors contribute g(u) and the spherical Hessian along w, with no cross term or angular acceleration term.

At the witness orientation the φ″ term vanishes because dp_K=0. The remaining line second derivative is φ(α)−|φ′(α)| times the realization multiplier, with φ(α) added once, i.e. φ(α)−|φ′(α)|·2^k/(3V). It is strictly negative for sufficiently large multiplier. Local C² regularity at the orientation suffices.

dependencies.hypotheses_mapping: k=d−1, α chosen in (0,1) with φ′(α)≠0, and A=−sign(φ′(α))I_k satisfy the realization hypotheses. Its centered stationary section, analytic local cap fraction, and unbounded positive Hessian multiplier supply all witness properties.

overlap.comparison: Constructs a metronoid support function from directional moments of fixed-mass caps. It imposes no universal scalar transform of the variable through-origin cap fraction and does not give the obstruction.

readability: The tangent great-circle parametrization keeps the curvature test at the realized cap direction. No global C² property of the cap fraction is needed.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The same-batch realization supplies an actual stationary orientation with the prescribed fraction and diverging curvature of the required sign. The support function convexity test fails along a tangent line there.
